methods.label: Count matching rotation classes

annotationRationale: Rotational equivalence determines the favorable outcomes. Counting face subsets gives the class sizes, and each class contributes the square of its size to the equally likely ordered-pair sample space.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no area change is proposed.

review.questionCheck: With independent equiprobable face colors, there are 4096 ordered painting pairs. The rotation-class sizes are 1, 6, 3, 12, 8, 12, 3, 12, 6, 1; their squared sizes sum to 588. The probability is 147/1024, choice D. No stem, choice, key, or figure contradiction appears.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods are supplied. The candidate retains the useful rotation-class approach from both LIVE and AoPS. A conditional-probability presentation would repeat the same classification, and no additional accessible route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Symmetry counting and classical probability are central assessed concepts. Combination counts and multiplication appropriately support the class sizes and ordered-pair counts. No unsupported contextual concepts are added.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no area change is proposed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The class sizes sum to 64. Two black faces give opposite and adjacent classes of sizes 3 and 12. Three black faces either select one face from each opposite pair, yielding eight vertex paintings, or contain a unique opposite pair, yielding 3·4 = 12 paintings. Each type is rotationally equivalent internally. Summing m² gives 588 matching ordered pairs.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS are accurately credited as nonofficial sources for the class-size and squared-size argument. The candidate supplies original explanation of the sample space and three-face classification, rather than reproducing the third-party prose.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation establishes why class sizes must be squared and why each nontrivial class is complete. The opposite-pair argument resolves the difficult three-black-face case without relying on a picture or unexplained orbit terminology.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:symmetry-counting captures rotational equivalence and unequal class sizes; cnm_h137 supplies the equally likely probability model; cnm_h237 and cnm_h231 support subset and ordered-pair counts. All IDs are used appropriately.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native-topic links for classical probability, combination counts, and multiplication fit. The symmetry-class synthesis has no accepted CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower S-CP.B.9 and partial 7.SP.C.8a links support combination-based compound probability. They do not cover the rotational classification, and the other supplied nodes have no accepted US links.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The mapping captures both the central symmetry classification and the finite probability calculation. No advanced orbit-counting theorem is assumed.
